title: Month-3 Transition Check and separation of new graduate nurses within 12 months of hire
subtitle: Diagnostic accuracy study within a hospital nurse residency program
statement: Between 19 and 26 percent of each residency intake leave the hospital within 12 months of hire. The residency collects a 15-item Transition Check at month 3 but does not know whether a score of 30 or below identifies the residents who will later leave. The study will estimate the sensitivity and specificity of that cut-off against separation within 12 months of hire before a mentoring booster is tied to it.
whoAffected: New graduate registered nurses in the residency (about 210 a year in three intakes), their preceptors and nurse educators, the units that lose staff, and the patients those units care for.
whatHurts: Each early separation loses months of orientation and preceptor time and leaves units short of experienced nurses. Residents who struggle are not offered help in time, and a poorly performing cut-off would either miss them or label many residents who were never going to leave.
currentPractice: The Transition Check is completed at the month-3 seminar and filed without action; retention support is the same for every resident, and separation is tracked only in annual human resources summaries.
whyNow: The educators want to launch a mentoring booster with the October 2026 intake, and the ethics approval and the human resources data release are already in place.
constraints: No research funding beyond the residency budget. The Transition Check is completed during the month-3 seminar and must add no extra resident time. Scores are never shared with nurse managers or used in performance reviews. Human resources can release hire and separation dates only, not exit reasons.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients on every unit are cared for by supported, experienced nurses because residents who are struggling are offered help early without being labelled or judged.
summary: Problem framed as a diagnostic accuracy question: does a month-3 score of 30 or below identify residents who separate within 12 months of hire?
